policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'beloved in God the Father', rendering the perfect passive of agapao; the RP variant 'sanctified' (hegiasmenois) is nowhere in the verse or its notes. The two alternative_rendering notes concern 'Jacob' and the participle order, not the lemma.
ASV renders the pronoun: 'of our common salvation'. The RP omission would leave 'the common salvation' with no possessive.

ASV reads 'denying our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ' with no 'God' before 'Master'; the RP addition of theon is unrendered. The alternative_rendering note only redistributes 'our' between Master and Lord.

ASV 'though ye know all things once for all' renders hapax but supplies the participle's subject as 'ye' whether or not the redundant humas stands, and English cannot reproduce the transposition of humas and hapax. NA's omission of hapax here is offset by the hapax its reading carries in the adjacent kurios unit, so no candidate is excluded.
ASV reads 'though ye know all things' (panta); the RP touto would give 'know this'.

The mapped textual_variant note 'Many very ancient authorities read Jesus' puts Iesous in the margin, so the ASV text is kurios and the base reading is excluded. ASV cannot distinguish the article (kurios vs ho kurios), both giving 'the Lord'. NA's ho kurios hapax is excluded because ASV places 'once for all' with 'ye know all things', not with the Lord's saving.
The variants differ only in the order of tropon and toutois; ASV's 'having in like manner with these' renders both words and word order is not recoverable from the English.
The variant is the presence of the article hoi alone, which ASV's 'they who are hidden rocks in your love-feasts' neither renders nor excludes.

ASV 'to convict all the ungodly of all their works of ungodliness': 'all the ungodly' matches pantas tous asebeis, the single 'their' belongs to ergon asebeias auton outside this unit so RP's added auton is unrendered, and NA's 'every soul' (pasan psuchen) is absent.
ASV reads the plain possessive 'walking after their lusts'; the reflexive heauton would be rendered 'their own', as ASV does render it a few lines later in this same book.

The variant hoti is recitative, introducing direct speech; ASV renders the speech directly ('they said to you, In the last time...'), which is what both readings yield, so the English does not show whether hoti stood.
All three readings mean 'in the last time'; the article and the ep' + genitive vs en + dative construction are not distinguishable in ASV's 'In the last time'.
The readings differ only in whether the participial phrase precedes or follows 'on your most holy faith'; ASV renders every word and English order does not settle the Greek.

ASV's text reads 'on some have mercy', and the mapped note relegates the refuting reading to the margin ('Some ancient authorities read And some refute'), so Treg's elenchete is excluded. eleate and eleeite are orthographic forms of the same verb and both give 'have mercy'.

ASV renders three distinct groups across 1:22-23 -- 'on some have mercy, who are in doubt' (accusative diakrinomenous as the object of eleate), 'and some save, snatching them out of the fire', 'and on some have mercy with fear'. That three-clause shape excludes r02 (WH), which lacks the second 'ous de' and so folds the rescued into the doubters, and excludes r03 (RP), which has nominative diakrinomenoi and only two groups with no closing 'have mercy with fear' clause; the ASV note reports the r03 sense ('some refute while they dispute with you', cf. the alternative rendering 'while they dispute with you') as what other authorities read, i.e. not the text translated. r00-base and r01 are the same words and differ only in comma placement, which the English cannot distinguish, so the unit stays underdetermined between them and the base fallback carries the projection.
ASV reads the second person throughout: 'able to guard you from stumbling, and to set you before'; RP's autous would give 'them'.
ASV reads 'to the only God our Saviour' with no 'wise'; RP's added sopho would give 'the only wise God'.
ASV renders the phrase in full: 'through Jesus Christ our Lord'; RP omits it.
ASV's list is asyndetic until the last member, 'glory, majesty, dominion and power', matching doxa megalosune kratos kai exousia; RP's added kai after doxa would give 'glory and majesty'.
ASV renders the phrase: 'before all time, and now, and for evermore'; RP omits pro pantos tou aionos.
